active_scientific_question: How repeatedly and how deeply did capitulum traits differentiate, and do independently bounded differentiation windows share a robust historical environmental or range-reorganization context?

phyllary_posture.reading: recurrent with relatively deeper placements admissible

recurrence_and_depth.shared_transition_localization: 0/3 discrete trait pairs pass the robust rule

calendar_identifiability.best_resolved_event: core-Nipponocirsium erect/upward to nodding/downward orientation transition
calendar_identifiability.consequence: repeated same-trait historical-trigger inference remains not_evaluable because multiple trait-changing branches cannot currently be calendarized from public machine-readable phylogenies

orientation_historical_environment.central_pair_tendency: BIO1, BIO4 and BIO15 decrease in all four regions; BIO12 increases in three of four
orientation_historical_environment.boundary: central-age tendencies are not historical-trigger evidence after chronology and paleolocation uncertainty are propagated

lineage_level_climate_context.analysis_scope: lineage-diversification context only; not capitulum-trait transition trigger
lineage_level_climate_context.reading: Pleistocene climate is a broad backdrop, but no single tested climate regime recurs robustly across representative lineage differentiations

global_sea_level_context.analysis_scope: range-reorganization context only; not local island connectivity and not a trait-transition test
global_sea_level_context.boundary: global eustatic reconstruction cannot rule out local Taiwan/Ryukyu/Japan connectivity or fragmentation

mid_pleistocene_context.reading: MPT overlap is broad era context largely implied by the chronology envelope, not independent trigger evidence

module_trigger_status.orientation: historical climate and global sea-level trigger unresolved after full uncertainty propagation; repeated trigger not evaluable with one dateable transition
module_trigger_status.flower_colour: dated conditional white-lineage branch envelopes exist, but ancestral colour and exact transition timing remain conditional and historical radiative trigger is not evaluable
module_trigger_status.phyllary_posture: recurrent and relatively deep, but transition-bearing calendar chronology is not available
module_trigger_status.stickiness: recurrent and shallow, but dated range events are not stickiness-transition ages
module_trigger_status.whole_capitulum: one universal synchronized historical trigger is not supported; complete independence is not demonstrated

scientific_reading: Public evidence resolves repeated capitulum differentiation and unequal evolutionary depth substantially better than it resolves historical cause. Neither the best-bounded orientation event nor a broader set of representative lineage-differentiation windows identifies one robust recurring tested BIOCLIM or global eustatic sea-level trigger. This does not imply that climate, local geographic fragmentation, biotic interactions or selection were irrelevant; several of those processes remain unmeasured or not event-identifiable at the necessary scale.

dissertation_handoff.chapter2: freeze differentiation history and the current failure to identify one recurring tested historical trigger under public-data uncertainty
dissertation_handoff.later_synthesis: only then assess retained, lost, reversed or switched environmental domains between differentiation and maintenance
dissertation_handoff.chapter3: test ancestry-linked environment to trait function to reproductive fitness before any adaptive claim

claim_boundary: Minimum-change counts are lower bounds and do not establish independent origins or convergence.
Relative lineage depth is not calendar time.
Lineage divergence or dispersal ages are not automatically trait-transition ages.
Regional paleolocation boxes are sensitivity scenarios, not ancestral-area probabilities.
No robust recurring tested climate or global sea-level context does not mean historical environment was biologically irrelevant.
Global eustatic sea level does not reconstruct local island connectivity.
Historical alignment would remain observational and would not establish natural selection or adaptation.
Adaptation requires Chapter 3 mechanism and reproductive-fitness evidence.
